First, I came home from college in Britain, which is like being in high school in America. My mom told me that my great aunt Wyndy died, and the funeral will probably be soon. My initial thoughts were confusionâĢĶ'Who?' and 'Why is she telling me this?' I had never heard of this name before, and I don't remember meeting this person except maybe once when I was really young, like 1 or 2 years old. This led to an argument with my mom. She wanted me to go to the funeral, even though I'm really awkward at funerals, especially for people I've only met once or don't know well. I ended up saying, "Fine, I'll go on my own," in a sulkier tone. Her main arguments for me going were about respect and support for her, even though she's never mentioned this great aunt to me before, despite supposedly playing a big role in raising her. She also mentioned that it's one of the few times we'll see the much larger branch of the family, where there might be hundreds of us, but I've only seen about 10 of them more than once, maybe not even that many. To me, it feels like gate-crashing someone else's family funeral, even though I'm part of the family. I don't know the person who died, and I don't think anyone else would want me there since I don't know or didn't know the person who died. I'm trying to understand if it's morally acceptable for me not to attend this funeral. I've never met this person beyond that one time when I was a baby, and the name has never been mentioned to me before now. So, is it wrong for me to not want to go to the funeral of someone who is practically a stranger to me, just because she's family? I think about respect and support. My mom says I should go out of respect and to support her. But if I don't know the person, how can I truly respect them or support her in this context? It feels more like an obligation to attend a family event rather than a genuine expression of grief or support. Also, considering the size of the family, it's likely that there will be many people there, but I don't know most of them. Attending might make me feel out of place or like an outsider, which could be uncomfortable for me. On the other hand, family is important, and attending funerals is often seen as a way to honor the deceased and support the grieving family. But in this case, since I don't know the person or the family well, it's hard to see how my presence would make a difference. I'm also thinking about the concept of duty versus personal comfort. Is it my duty to attend just because I'm family, even if I feel awkward or uncomfortable? Or is it more important to honor my own feelings and boundaries? I wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I could send a card or a message expressing my condolences instead of attending in person. That way, I'm showing respect without feeling like I'm gate-crashing or being uncomfortable. But then, my mom might feel hurt or think that I don't care if I don't attend. How do I balance my own feelings with her expectations? I also think about the cultural and familial expectations around funerals. In some cultures, attending funerals is a significant obligation, and not doing so could be seen as disrespectful. But in my case, since I don't know the person or the family well, it's unclear how strong that obligation is. Overall, I'm torn between respecting family traditions and honoring my own feelings and comfort. I need to decide whether not attending is morally acceptable in this situation.
